title: Social Proof

scenes.text: One sentence got more people to *reuse towels*
scenes.vo: Changing one sentence on a card got way more hotel guests to reuse their towels.

scenes.text:
Card A:
“Please help save the planet”
scenes.vo: Card A said: please help save the planet, reuse your towel.

scenes.text:
Card B:
“*Most guests* here reuse their towels”
scenes.vo: Card B just said: most guests in this hotel reuse their towels.
Card B won. More people reused their towels when they knew others did it too.
This is called social proof. When we're not sure what to do, we copy what other people are doing.

scenes.text:
Views. Likes. “Bestseller.”
The long queue outside a shop.
scenes.vo: It's why videos with lots of views get even more views, and why a long queue makes you think the food must be good.

scenes.text: Before you follow the crowd, ask: do *I* actually want this?
scenes.vo: So before you follow the crowd, ask yourself: do I actually want this, or is everyone else just doing it?

caption:
We copy the crowd way more than we think. 🏨 It's called social proof.

What's the last thing you bought because everyone had it? 👇
source: Goldstein, N. J., Cialdini, R. B. & Griskevicius, V. (2008). A Room with a Viewpoint. Journal of Consumer Research, 35(3).
